name: slide_write
description: Write one slide into the deck as its generator builds slides (lift-up FUNC-1), from a slide in the JSON Narrato writes (`deck_generate`'s `slides`): its layout chosen for its items, each place filled, its figures, builds, and icons, in the deck's theme and the brief it keeps. After the slide that holds `after`, in place of the slide that holds `replace` (its beat kept, its picture shown again, the nodes no other slide shows taken away with it), or at the end. Its `speakerNotes` are its first state's own wherever the beat it joins keeps notes of its own, so a presenter reads them on it. Its states join `beat`, a beat of the spine whose claim it tells (plan the spine with `spine_update` first), which keeps what it says; with none, it gets a beat of its own, and a deck with no spine yet begins one, the slide taking the place of `deck_create`'s blank slide. Its set of texts held to one size and lint's fixes taken, as a made deck's are; what no fix mends is in `left`, a text past its place first. One patch, refused as `deck_patch` refuses one, reported as `deck_patch` reports one (`summary`, and the JSON Patch only with `verbose`), with the slide's states, layout, and beat.

bundle.description: The bundle: a directory, a `.scaena` zip, or a `deck.json`.

slide.description:
One slide, as Narrato writes each of `deck_generate`'s `slides`: `slideTitle`, `subtitle`,
`layoutSuggestion`, `keyBullets`, `speakerNotes`, and `chartData`, `icons`, `beatName`,
`purpose`, `intent`, `expectedIntensity`, and `expectedValence` where it has them.

after.description: The slide goes after the slide that holds this state.

replace.description:
The slide is written in place of the slide that holds this state, with all its steps, in
its beat. Without it or `after`, the slide goes after every slide.

beat.description:
The id of a beat of the spine whose claim this slide tells, as `spine_update` planned it:
the slide's states join it, and it keeps its claim, evidence, and notes, the slide giving
only what it lacks (Narrato's fields); the slide's own `speakerNotes` go on its first
state, which a presenter reads before the beat's; without `after`, the slide stands where the spine plans it,
after that beat's slides, else after the nearest earlier beat's, else before the nearest
later beat's. Without it, the slide gets a beat of its own after the slide
before it, and a deck with no spine yet begins one. Not with `replace`, which keeps the
beat of the slide it takes the place of.

dry_run.description: Say what would change, and write nothing.

verbose.description:
The patch compiled to JSON Patch too (`patch`), which a slide makes long: every state of
the deck, as `deck_patch`'s `verbose` gives it.

Summary.description:
What a patch changed in a deck's slides, each by the id of its first state, and in its
spine's beats, each by its id: what was added, taken away, moved among the rest, or, a beat,
told otherwise (its claim, states, evidence, notes, or time). Each list is in the deck's order,
and left out when empty.

json_patch.description: How many of the ops given were JSON Patch.

oneOf.description:
Put `value` at `path`: a member of an object (one already there is replaced, in its
place), or an item of an array, at an index or at its end (`-`).
Replace what is at `path`, which must be there.

`remove` at `from`, then `add` at `path`. A member moved within its object keeps its
place: a rename.
Fail the patch unless `path` holds `value` (numbers equal by value: 1 is 1.0).

Pointer.description:
A JSON Pointer (RFC 6901): empty, the whole document, or `/`-separated tokens, `~1` for a
`/` and `~0` for a `~` inside one.

Finding.description: One lint finding, shaped for agents: a code, a JSON pointer, and (when safe) a fix.

file.description: The bundle file `path` points into, when it is not `deck.json` (a theme file).

format.description: The format the deck was laid out in (`"9:16"`), when it is not the deck's own.

fix.description: A JSON Patch (RFC 6902) that resolves the finding. Only safe, non-content fixes.

refresh.description:
The data source to fetch again, where what resolves the finding is a fetch, which no patch
makes (W428, ADR-0030): the source's name, without its `@`.

Restated.description:
A beat whose claim its slide said before an edit and says no more: what it claimed, what the
slide says now, and the patch that sets the claim to it.

state.description: The state of the beat's slide whose words `says` are, or, with none, the beat's first.

path.description: Where the claim is, as a JSON pointer.

claim.description: The claim, as the beat still says it.

says.description:
What the slide says now: the words of the text that said the claim, in the state it said
it in, else the last that shows it; none where every such text was taken away.

fix.description:
The patch that sets the claim to what the slide says, where it says something: a `test`
of the old claim, then a `replace`.

Fell.description:
A slide whose `layoutSuggestion` could not be taken as asked (agent dogfood): the slide, by
its number from 1, what it asked, the layout it took, and why, so an agent can ask again.

applied.description: Whether the deck was written: not under a dry run, nor when the patch was refused.

ops.description:
The semantic ops given (SPEC §7.3), in order, as given; JSON Patch ops are counted in
`summary`.

summary.description: What changed in the deck's slides and its story.

patch.description: With `verbose`, the patch as RFC 6902, in order.

added.description: What `validate` and `lint` find after the patch that they did not before.

removed.description: What they found before that they do not after.

errors.description: The findings that are errors, after.

states.description: The states it changes, by id, as [`Patched`] says them.

restated.description:
Each beat whose claim its slide said before the patch and says no more, as [`Patched`]
says them (lift-up FUNC-2). Left out when none.

fell.description:
Its `layoutSuggestion`, where it could not be taken as asked: the slide, by its number in
the deck, what it asked, the layout it took, and why (agent dogfood).
